domains.scope_note: Housing starts reflect private/non-profit construction and senior-government policy as well as municipal approvals.
domains.interpretation_note: Use the budget line as municipal capacity context only; it is not a claim that planning spending caused housing starts.

domains.scope_note: Transit ridership and budget figures cover different reporting bases in some years; source labels are shown.
domains.interpretation_note: Ridership is a service-use outcome. Net requirement is the tax-supported operating context after service revenue, not cost per ride.

domains.scope_note: The longitudinal crime trend uses Statistics Canada’s Peterborough CMA for consistent boundaries. A separate PPS service-area CSI is shown as current local-service context; the two series are not combined.
domains.interpretation_note: Community F.I.R.S.T. activity measures show workload and outputs; they should not be treated as proof of broader crime reduction.

domains.scope_note: Asset-condition figures combine observed and age-based information. 2025 lane-kilometres are work outputs, not substitutes for a comparable annual network-condition outcome.
domains.interpretation_note: Condition and funding-gap measures help show the scale of the infrastructure challenge; they are not a one-year performance grade.

domains.scope_note: The City is Service Manager for Peterborough City and County. Social Services is much broader than homelessness spending.
domains.interpretation_note: Waitlists, housing placements and By-Name data describe system outcomes/pressure; they should not be attributed to a single City budget line.

trends.headline: Ahead cumulatively, uneven year to year
trends.summary: Peterborough reported 1,345 homes against a cumulative provincial target of 1,207 from 2023-2025 (111%). It exceeded target in 2023 and 2025 but reached 75% in 2024.
trends.methodology_note: Housing-progress targets are a provincial measurement framework and should not be read as a direct measure of municipal planning productivity.

trends.headline: Ridership has recovered from the 2023 level
trends.summary: Reported total ridership rose from 3,205,294 in 2023 to more than 3.7 million in 2025 — a minimum increase of about 15.4%. A 2018 historical reference of 4,973,571 is shown, but 2025 is published only as a rounded lower bound, so no exact recovery-to-peak percentage is claimed.
trends.methodology_note: Uses City-reported all-mode ridership. Comparability is stronger for 2023-2025 than for the older historical reference because service design and counting practices can change.

trends.headline: Regional Crime Severity Index is lower than in 2021
trends.summary: Statistics Canada’s Peterborough CMA CSI moved from 64.8 in 2021 to 57.3 in 2025, an 11.6% decline, with a small increase in 2024 before falling again in 2025. Lower is better.
trends.methodology_note: The longitudinal series uses the Peterborough CMA for consistent boundaries. The separate PPS service-area CSI is retained as a current service-area metric and should not be spliced into the CMA trend.

trends.headline: Current plan, old condition observation
trends.summary: The City has a 2025 Asset Management Plan, but key road-condition observations still rely on 2023 asset-condition data. That is useful structural context, not a current 2026 outcome reading.
trends.methodology_note: Infrastructure is intentionally excluded from the fresh-signal scorecard until a newer comparable network-condition observation is published. 2025 work delivered and funding-gap estimates remain available as context.

trends.headline: Latest system count rose 16% in 2025
trends.summary: The City reported a minimum of 932 people experienced homelessness in 2025, up from 803 in 2024 (+16%). The May 2026 shelter report also says demand continues to exceed the existing 127-bed emergency shelter/overnight system.
trends.methodology_note: This is the freshest City-reported system-pressure indicator available. It counts people connected to services who were unsheltered, sheltered or couch surfing; it is not a point-in-time count and should not be compared directly with older RGI waitlist totals.
